title: Improve downstream PostgreSQL test-suite performance
description:
## Verified audit

Audited git HEAD: 6edc72c. The worktree was clean before issue creation, Beads had no open work, and bv reported no duplicate suggestions.

Current evidence:
- Disposable creation and cleanup each open a new admin connection; every AdminClient builds a private Tokio runtime.
- Repeated template acquisition retains one shared-lock session per caller instead of caching a live per-server template.
- Explicit cleanup blocks the caller, while Drop fallback uses one process-global serial worker and retains the database permit until DROP finishes.
- Default capacity is floor(120 / 11) = 10 simultaneous database leases.
- Owned containers already disable fsync, synchronous_commit, and full_page_writes, but do not use initdb --no-sync or tmpfs.
- Testcontainers is always compiled, including external-server-only consumers.

Directional local measurements on cached postgres:18, Docker overlay2, 64 logical CPUs:
- 40 template0 create/comment/drop lifecycles: 1.16 s on one admin session versus 4.49 s with fresh create and cleanup sessions.
- pgbench SELECT: 0.156 ms persistent versus 9.13 ms reconnecting each transaction.
- Final TCP readiness: median 1.829 s current versus 1.306 s with initdb --no-sync.
- Twelve clone/drop cycles from a 40.5 MB template: 984 ms on the normal Docker volume versus 778 ms on tmpfs.
- FILE_COPY was slightly slower than default WAL_LOG for that template and is not accepted as a default optimization.

Accepted work tracks are the child issues. Explicit non-goals are enabling Testcontainers reusable-container mode, making trust authentication the default, weakening database-per-test isolation, or forcing FILE_COPY. Reduced-fidelity PostgreSQL settings require opt-in semantics and benchmark evidence.

## Success criteria

The project has reproducible performance characterization, fewer repeated setup costs, bounded cleanup and prewarming, a faster owned-container path, an external-only build, and actionable downstream guidance without weakening lifecycle safety.
acceptance_criteria: Every verified child is completed or closed with an evidence-backed rejection; benchmark results are recorded; database isolation, cleanup safety, and default public API behavior remain explicit.

title: PERF01: Add reproducible downstream performance characterization
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in, documented benchmark workflow reports cold startup, template acquisition, sequential and concurrent clone-cleanup throughput, admin connection churn, and owned versus external modes without adding flaky wall-clock assertions to the normal test suite.
close_reason: Completed reproducible owned/external characterization workflow, baseline, failure-safe lifecycle, deadline handling, atomic output, random namespaces, and precise content-ID provenance.

title: Harden PERF01 characterization after comprehensive review
description: Address retained comprehensive-review findings in the performance example: make lifecycle mode authoritative, bound observer I/O, back off external cleanup retries, and encode measurement/provenance semantics explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: Each retained finding has a root-cause-driven fix in a separate green commit; schema and docs describe methodology; the complete Rust and Docker validation suite passes.

title: PERF02: Reuse a bounded pool of disposable-lifecycle admin sessions
description:
## Verified finding

src/harness.rs creates a fresh admin connection for every disposable database at create_test_database and another in DatabaseLeaseInner::cleanup. connect_admin constructs an AdminClient, and AdminClient::connect builds a private current-thread Tokio runtime, performs TCP and PostgreSQL authentication, spawns the connection task, and configures session timeouts.

Directional measurements:
- 40 template0 create/comment/drop lifecycles took 1.16 s using one session and 4.49 s using fresh create and cleanup sessions.
- pgbench averaged 0.156 ms per SELECT on a persistent connection and 9.13 ms when reconnecting each transaction.

The exact speedup inside Rust must be established by PERF01, but repeated connection and runtime construction is confirmed.

## Target

Add a lazy, bounded admin-session pool owned by ServerInner for disposable CREATE-COMMENT and DROP operations. Size it from an explicit policy tied to lifecycle concurrency and PostgreSQL headroom. Checkouts must be exclusive without holding the pool mutex during SQL work.

Keep retained owner and template advisory-lock sessions outside the reusable pool. Restore required session timeout state before reuse. Evict and replace sessions after protocol, connection, or uncertain session-state failures. Do not serialize all database creation and cleanup through one client.

## Guardrails and validation

Preserve create/tag compensation, detached spawn_blocking result cleanup, operation timeout errors, owned shutdown admission, and external mode. Add tests for reuse, pool bounds, concurrent progress, backend termination and reconnection, cancellation, poisoned-session eviction, and shutdown. Use pg_stat_activity or connection instrumentation to prove the pool bound and PERF01 to compare throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Disposable CREATE-COMMENT and DROP operations reuse a lazy bounded per-server admin-session pool; concurrency is not globally serialized; broken sessions are evicted; timeout and cancellation semantics are preserved; integration tests and the performance benchmark demonstrate lower connection churn.

title: PERF03: Single-flight and cache live templates per server
description:
## Verified finding

Every PostgresHarness::template call runs begin_template through spawn_blocking and opens a retained PersistentClient. Even when the same fingerprint is already live in the same ServerInner, a new TemplateInner and shared advisory-lock session are created.

The integration suite confirms eight concurrent callers initialize once but deliberately expects eight additional ShareLock sessions. DatabaseTemplate::clone itself already shares one Arc and is cheap, so repeated template() calls are the avoidable path.

## Target

Add a per-ServerInner, fingerprint-keyed successful-template cache with single-flight initialization. Same-fingerprint callers in one server should await one initialization and receive handles backed by the same TemplateInner. Use weak ownership or another cycle-free design so cache state does not keep the server or template alive unintentionally.

On initializer error or cancellation, remove or transition the in-flight entry so a later caller can recover and use its own initializer. Preserve PostgreSQL advisory-lock coordination between distinct ServerInner values and processes.

## Guardrails and validation

Characterize and update N-way cold start, queued exclusive waiter fairness, initializer error recovery, initializer cancellation recovery, separate template-wait timeout behavior, shared-lock release after the final clone, and owned shutdown. Add warm-path assertions for one retained session and no extra catalog/lock round trips. Compare cold and warm acquisition with PERF01.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent and repeated same-fingerprint calls on one ServerInner share one live TemplateInner and retained shared-lock session; only one initializer runs; failure and cancellation cannot strand cache state; cross-server advisory-lock coordination and template lifetime safety remain covered.

title: PERF04: Add bounded deferred cleanup with an explicit drain barrier
description:
## Verified finding

DatabaseLease::cleanup waits for a new admin connection and FORCE DROP before returning. DatabaseLease::drop sends DatabaseLeaseInner to one process-global DATABASE_CLEANUP_WORKER, which cleans every server and project serially. The OwnedSemaphorePermit remains inside DatabaseLeaseInner until cleanup finishes, so queued database requests cannot proceed even after the consumer has closed its application pool and returned the lease.

This is a confirmed critical-path and head-of-line-blocking seam. Any change must retain observable cleanup failures and bound residual databases.

## Target

Introduce a bounded, server-scoped deferred cleanup facility using the pooled admin sessions from PERF02. Provide an explicit asynchronous drain or shutdown barrier that waits for queued work and reports failures. Preserve the current awaited cleanup path for callers that require immediate confirmation; add a clearly named deferred return path or documented policy rather than silently discarding errors.

Define when the per-database connection permit is released. The contract may release it when a consumer explicitly returns the lease after closing all application pools, but must bound cleanup concurrency and queued residual databases so PostgreSQL connection and storage limits cannot be overrun.

## Guardrails and validation

Cover explicit success and failure, deferred success and failure reporting, queue saturation/backpressure, multiple harnesses, cancellation, Drop fallback, owned shutdown, external server lifetime, active application connections, permit handoff, and process teardown. No database may be reused without being recreated from the immutable template. PERF01 must record caller latency and final drain time.
acceptance_criteria: The harness offers bounded server-scoped deferred cleanup and an awaited drain that reports failures; cleanup is not globally serialized; database permits and shutdown ordering follow a documented safe contract; explicit cleanup behavior remains available and all lifecycle tests pass.

title: PERF05: Add opt-in prewarmed disposable database queues
description:
## Verified finding

Each DatabaseTemplate::database call synchronously acquires permits and performs CREATE DATABASE from the immutable template before returning a URL. For short downstream tests, the measured clone floor can dominate the test body even after admin sessions are pooled.

PostgreSQL has no portable constant-time snapshot or safe generic reset for arbitrary pools and extensions. Precreating clean clones and replacing returned databases is feasible without weakening database-level isolation.

## Target

Add an opt-in, bounded prewarmed queue associated with a DatabaseTemplate or a new pool abstraction. Prewarm clean databases from the template, hand out only never-used clones, and after return drop the dirty database and create a fresh replacement in the background.

Idle prewarmed databases must not hold application-connection permits. Acquire capacity atomically when leasing; retain the idle database if admission is closed or unavailable. Bound ready, creating, and deleting counts to cap disk or tmpfs consumption.

## Guardrails and validation

Never truncate and reuse a dirty database. Preserve unique names, metadata tagging, cancellation compensation, external stale-cleanup safety, template shared-lock lifetime, and owned shutdown. Test refill failures, queue exhaustion, concurrent leases, cancellation, multiple templates, drain behavior, and resource bounds. PERF01 must report first-lease latency, steady-state latency, refill throughput, and storage growth.
acceptance_criteria: An opt-in bounded prewarm API can prepare clean databases per template, lease them without reusing dirty state, refill after return, and shut down without leaked resources; idle databases do not consume application-connection permits; benchmark results quantify latency and storage tradeoffs.

title: PERF06: Add a fast and reliable owned-container storage profile
description:
## Verified finding

Owned containers currently pass fsync=off, synchronous_commit=off, full_page_writes=off, and max_connections=300, but do not set POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS or mount PostgreSQL storage on tmpfs.

The Docker Official postgres image supports POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS. PostgreSQL 18 documents initdb --no-sync as useful for testing. Testcontainers 0.27.3 exposes Mount::tmpfs_mount and ImageExt::with_mount. PostgreSQL 18's official image uses /var/lib/postgresql as the declared volume parent.

Local final-TCP-ready medians:
- current: 1.829 s;
- initdb --no-sync: 1.306 s, about 29 percent faster;
- no-sync plus tmpfs: 1.327 s, so tmpfs did not further improve startup.

For a 40.5 MB template, twelve clone/drop cycles took 984 ms on the normal volume and 778 ms on tmpfs, about 21 percent faster.

## Target

Add a coherent owned-container performance profile. Enable or expose initdb --no-sync for compatible owned images. Add configurable tmpfs storage with an explicit size cap and opt-out. Ensure readiness represents the final TCP-listening server, not the temporary server used by the image during initialization.

Treat --no-data-checksums, wal_level=minimal, and similar behavior-reducing settings as separate opt-ins unless representative benchmarks and compatibility tests justify them. Preserve custom-image support with documented capability expectations.

## Guardrails and validation

Test default and custom images, rootless or unsupported tmpfs behavior, memory exhaustion reporting, startup timeout cleanup, final readiness, container removal, and external mode unaffectedness. Record cold startup, migration, clone, and cleanup results through PERF01. Do not enable reusable-container mode or trust authentication by default.
acceptance_criteria: Owned-container startup supports verified initdb no-sync and bounded tmpfs configuration with reliable final-server readiness; defaults and opt-ins are documented; custom images and reduced-fidelity settings have explicit compatibility behavior; Docker lifecycle tests and benchmarks pass.
close_reason: Completed: added the default no-sync plus bounded-tmpfs owned profile, final TCP readiness and cleanup diagnostics, custom/external compatibility coverage, documentation, and schema-v5 benchmark evidence

title: PERF07: Characterize and expose effective database concurrency
description:
## Verified finding

HarnessConfig defaults to a connection budget of 120 and 11 permits per database, yielding ten simultaneous leases. The owned server separately hard-codes max_connections=300. Owner locks, template locks, lifecycle admin sessions, and external-server limits are not represented in a user-visible effective concurrency value.

The existing setters correctly enforce positive, order-independent overrides, but downstream users must infer lease parallelism and total their application pools manually.

## Target

Use PERF01 after admin pooling, template caching, and cleanup changes to characterize throughput across lease concurrency and downstream pool sizes. Expose the resolved budget, per-database permits, and effective maximum simultaneous leases through a stable read-only API or startup diagnostics.

Document that per-database permits cover the sum of all pools one test can open, and distinguish idle pool limits from actual eager connections. Evaluate whether owned max_connections should be derived from the configured budget plus explicit owner, template, admin-pool, and safety headroom. Change defaults only if representative results show a robust improvement.

## Guardrails and validation

Preserve 0 < per_database <= budget, builder order independence, terminal admission on owned shutdown, and external-server configurability. Test low-capacity servers, many templates, pool checkout spikes, superuser-reserved slots, and configurations larger than the owned server can safely support.
acceptance_criteria: Effective lease concurrency and its connection-pool formula are observable and documented; defaults or owned max_connections change only with benchmark evidence and explicit administrative headroom; existing configuration invariants and external-server safety remain tested.

title: PERF08: Feature-gate owned-container support for external-only builds
description:
## Verified finding

testcontainers is an unconditional normal dependency with blocking, ring, and watchdog features. A normal dependency-tree inspection found about 234 unique package-version entries beneath testcontainers. External-server consumers still compile this path even though ServerInner selects it only when no admin URL is configured.

Feature gating is feasible but not mechanical: src/server.rs contains all Testcontainers and libc::atexit use, while the public non-exhaustive Error enum exposes testcontainers::TestcontainersError in two variants. Default-feature API compatibility therefore needs explicit validation.

## Target

Introduce a default-enabled owned-container feature, with a clear name such as containers. Make testcontainers and container-only libc usage optional. With default features, preserve current behavior and public API. With owned-container support disabled, POSTGRES_TEST_ADMIN_URL or with_admin_database_url must work fully, while an attempt to start without an external URL returns a precise configuration error.

Decide and document the feature-specific shape of container error variants, HarnessConfig::with_image, container_id, and shutdown. Prefer keeping source compatibility in default builds.

## Guardrails and validation

Run cargo check, tests, rustdoc, MSRV, and public-API comparison under default features. Run check, tests, docs, and a real external PostgreSQL lifecycle under no-default-features. Prove through cargo tree that testcontainers, Bollard, Rustls/Ring pulled only by the container path, and container-only libc are absent where possible. Measure clean compile impact through PERF01.
acceptance_criteria: Default features preserve owned-container behavior and public API compatibility; a documented external-only build excludes testcontainers and container-only dependencies, requires an admin URL with a clear error otherwise, and passes check, tests, docs, and dependency-tree verification.

title: PERF09: Publish a downstream test-suite performance guide and adapter
acceptance_criteria: Documentation includes a tested reusable adapter and CI examples covering one harness and template per process, one external server per job, stable fingerprints, pool and permit sizing, cleanup and drain semantics, performance profiles, external-only builds, and explicit unsafe non-recommendations.

title: Implement validated codebase simplifications from audit 473d280
description:
Canonical simplification audit for tracked commit 473d280772672a435cafd81901eee6e6db0f32e4.

Coverage contract
- 21/21 subsystem rows completed.
- Recommend: S02, S07, S08, S09, S10, S11, S12, S13, S14, S15.
- Explicit skip: S01, S03, S04, S05, S06, S16, S17, S18, S19, S20, S21.
- 12 accepted findings after independent coverage, overlap, materiality, schema, and dependency-ranking passes.

Ranked findings
1. S08-A exact Option<DatabaseRecord> lookup.
2. S14 lexical cleanup phase and exact test oracle.
3. S13 locked reread/reclassification for stale cleanup.
4. S08-B create/tag compensation owner.
5. S12 return DatabaseLease directly and remove CancellationGuard.
6. S15-A make postgres dev-only.
7. S07 direct per-client Tokio runtime shutdown.
8. S10 paired container-worker terminal state.
9. S09 close admission on owned shutdown.
10. S11 lock-before-inspect, same-session coordination.
11. S02 resolve connection-limit overrides once.
12. S15-B unify direct sha2 dependency on 0.11.

Dependency model
- S08-A and S14 block S13.
- S08-A and S07 block S11.
- S10 blocks S09.
- S08-B should precede S12 to avoid rewriting the same closure.
- S15-A should precede S07 to reduce overlapping admin/error edits.
- S02 requires a documented builder-semantics decision.
- S11 requires concurrency characterization.
- S15-B requires golden fingerprint and advisory-key vectors.

Explicitly rejected or deferred
- Standalone TemplateIdentity, generic background-worker abstraction, generic advisory-lock guard, separate S11/S13 catalog-state enums, generic framed-SHA helper, TemplateSpec removal, HeldClient oneshot rewrite, timestamp helper, and unused public error removal.
- Admin-URL dbname hardening, MissingUuidV7 error classification, and advisory-unlock result checking are behavior-hardening concerns outside this simplification audit.

Audit constraints and provenance
- Static/read-only audit; tests, builds, formatting, Clippy, implementation, commits, and pushes were not run.
- Every finding was independently rechecked against HEAD.
- PostgreSQL CREATE DATABASE and advisory-lock semantics were checked against PostgreSQL 18 documentation.
- At audit completion the tracked worktree/index were unchanged. Untracked .beads/ and AGENTS.md were outside the original tracked snapshot.

Use the child issues as the authoritative implementation backlog. Preserve behavior unless a child explicitly identifies and characterizes a behavior correction.

## Success Criteria
All child findings are either implemented and validated or explicitly closed with a documented rejection reason. Hard dependencies and characterization gates are honored. Public API, persisted identity, concurrency, and lifecycle behavior receive the validation specified on each child issue.
acceptance_criteria: All child findings are either implemented and validated or explicitly closed with a documented rejection reason. Hard dependencies and characterization gates are honored. Public API, persisted identity, concurrency, and lifecycle behavior receive the validation specified on each child issue.
close_reason: Completed: all 12 validated simplification findings were implemented in dependency order and passed their required behavior, concurrency, identity, stable, MSRV, documentation, and Docker checks

title: S08-A: Preserve catalog states with one exact database lookup
description:
## Verdict
Recommend. Audit rank 1. High impact, high confidence, low effort, low blast radius.

## Evidence
- src/admin.rs:75-78 already defines DatabaseRecord { name, comment }.
- src/admin.rs:333-356 performs separate database_exists and database_comment queries.
- database_comment flattens an absent row and a present row with NULL comment into the same None.
- src/harness.rs:327-348 issues both catalog queries during template initialization.
- src/admin.rs:424-438 already maps list results into DatabaseRecord.

## Current complexity
Existence and metadata come from two snapshots, while Option<String> loses the distinction between absent, present/untagged, and present/tagged databases.

## Target
Replace both private queries with find_database -> Result<Option<DatabaseRecord>>. None means absent; Some { comment: None } means present and untagged. Reuse this catalog shape in template inspection and stale cleanup; do not add parallel database-state enums.

## Scope and risks
Private changes in src/admin.rs and template/cleanup call sites in src/harness.rs. Preserve conservative handling of untagged databases, error context, and ready/recovery semantics.

## Validation
Retain unknown-template and cleanup coverage. Add direct cases for absent, present/NULL, present/tagged, recoverable Initializing, and Ready records.

## Acceptance Criteria
A single exact-name query represents all three catalog states; database_exists/database_comment duplication is removed from affected callers; untagged databases remain conservatively protected; focused tri-state and existing integration coverage pass.
acceptance_criteria: A single exact-name query represents all three catalog states; database_exists/database_comment duplication is removed from affected callers; untagged databases remain conservatively protected; focused tri-state and existing integration coverage pass.
close_reason: Implemented one exact-name Option<DatabaseRecord> lookup, updated template inspection/recovery callers, added direct catalog-state coverage, and passed unit plus Docker lifecycle tests.

title: S11: Inspect template state under locks on one retained session
description:
## Verdict
Conditionally recommend after characterization. Audit rank 10. Medium-high impact, medium confidence, medium-high effort, high concurrency blast radius.

## Evidence
- src/harness.rs:303-369 performs readiness probes, opens a second session, acquires exclusive lock, and may loop.
- src/harness.rs:398-424 reads before and after acquiring shared lock.
- src/harness.rs:265-289 publishes Ready, releases and drops exclusive ownership, then reconnects for shared ownership.
- Mandatory shared/exclusive locks are nullable at lines 150-155 and 256-269.

## Current complexity
Unlocked optimistic reads, protected rereads, discarded sessions, retries, and never-valid None states obscure one lock-protected lifecycle.

## Target
Use one session per attempt: acquire shared then inspect; on miss release shared, acquire exclusive and inspect; after publishing Ready release exclusive, acquire shared on the same session, then revalidate. Make live shared and consuming exclusive lock fields mandatory. Never request shared while still holding exclusive. Do not revive TemplateIdentity or a generic lock guard.

## Scope and risks
Private template coordination in src/harness.rs, consuming S08-A and S07 while retaining S19's primitive helpers. Preserve advisory lock counts/session identity, queue fairness, timeout restoration, cancellation, unlock behavior, and error timing.

## Validation
Before implementation add N-way cold start, queued-exclusive waiter, initializer error/cancellation recovery, timeout characterization, cleanup across template clones, and pg_locks inspection.

## Acceptance Criteria
Characterization tests exist before substitution; authoritative metadata reads occur under the intended lock; one session is retained through each coordination attempt; mandatory lock fields cannot be empty; no starvation, leaked lock, timeout regression, or duplicate initialization is observed.
acceptance_criteria: Characterization tests exist before substitution; authoritative metadata reads occur under the intended lock; one session is retained through each coordination attempt; mandatory lock fields cannot be empty; no starvation, leaked lock, timeout regression, or duplicate initialization is observed.
close_reason: Completed: one-session lock-protected template coordination with characterized starvation and recovery behavior

title: S02: Resolve connection-limit overrides into one validated value
description:
## Verdict
Conditionally recommend after freezing public builder semantics. Audit rank 11. Medium impact/confidence, low-medium effort, medium blast radius.

## Evidence
- src/config.rs:65-76 stores concrete budget/per-database values plus two provenance booleans.
- src/config.rs:136-169 interprets and mutates them through two order-sensitive builders.
- src/server.rs:108-120 builds a semaphore and requests per-database permits.
- src/config.rs:325-359 covers only some setter orders.

## Current complexity
Lowering then raising the budget leaves an implicitly clamped value sticky. with_connections_per_database(121) alone bypasses the default 120-budget check and can wait indefinitely for more permits than the semaphore contains.

## Target
Store raw optional nonzero overrides and resolve them once into a ResolvedConnectionLimits value before constructing ServerInner. Keep public builder signatures. A wrapper around the existing values/booleans is insufficient because it merely relocates the branching.

## Scope and risks
src/config.rs, src/server.rs, configuration tests, and README if behavior changes. First decide repeated-builder, default-clamping, validation-timing, and Debug-output semantics.

## Validation
Cover per-database-only 121, both setter orders, repeated lower/raise sequences, resolved defaults, zero/range errors, Debug output, and runtime permit capacity.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Build HarnessConfig::new("example").with_connections_per_database(121) without setting an explicit budget.
2. Observe configuration succeeds although the effective default connection budget is 120.
3. Start the harness and request a database.
4. Observe acquire_many_owned requests 121 permits from a semaphore initialized with 120 and cannot make progress. A separate sequence that lowers then raises the implicit budget also demonstrates sticky clamping.

## Acceptance Criteria
The intended builder-order/repetition contract is documented first; raw overrides have one resolution point; every resolved value satisfies 0 < per_database <= budget; invalid standalone configurations cannot reach permit acquisition; compatibility cases are tested.
acceptance_criteria: The intended builder-order/repetition contract is documented first; raw overrides have one resolution point; every resolved value satisfies 0 < per_database <= budget; invalid standalone configurations cannot reach permit acquisition; compatibility cases are tested.
close_reason: Completed: raw order-independent overrides resolve once into validated runtime connection limits

title: S15-B: Align the direct SHA-2 dependency with version 0.11
description:
## Verdict
Recommend as low-priority dependency maintenance. Audit rank 12. Low impact, low effort, medium persistent-identity blast radius; high confidence only after golden vectors.

## Evidence
- Cargo.toml:17 selects sha2 0.10.
- Cargo.lock:1873-1892 contains sha2 0.10.9 and 0.11.0 plus duplicate digest/block-buffer/crypto-common generations.
- src/fingerprint.rs:53-75 produces public template fingerprints.
- src/admin.rs:441-449 derives advisory keys.
- Existing tests establish relational properties, not exact known outputs.

## Current complexity
The normal graph carries two generations of the same SHA-256 implementation. The 0.10 chain appears to be owned only by this direct dependency.

## Target
First add known-answer vectors, then change the direct dependency to sha2 0.11 and regenerate Cargo.lock. Do not extract a generic framed-hash helper; fingerprint and advisory-key domains remain explicit.

## Scope and risks
Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock, with output validation owned by S03/S19. Any byte difference changes fingerprints, database names, persisted metadata, and lock keys.

## Validation
Record golden full-fingerprint and advisory-key outputs before the upgrade; require identical outputs afterward; run stable/MSRV/doc/Docker checks; verify legacy dependency nodes disappear.

title: S14: Give integration cleanup phases lexical resource ownership
description:
## Verdict
Recommend for test-state ownership only. Audit rank 2. Medium impact, high confidence, medium effort, test-only blast radius.

## Evidence
- tests/postgres.rs:19-350 is one end-to-end test.
- Handles from unrelated phases remain live when stale cleanup runs at lines 294-317.
- Cleanup assertions use lower bounds at lines 301-309.
- Manual resource teardown is concentrated at lines 337-349.

## Current complexity
Earlier phases silently affect later cleanup counts, weaken the oracle, and require manual lifetime bookkeeping.

## Target
Keep one amortized container test, but use lexical phases or phase reordering so the stale-cleanup phase has an exact known set: its intended active template, active database, and untagged lookalike. Use exact report assertions. Do not split every scenario into a separate container-starting test or extract cosmetic helpers.

## Scope and risks
tests/postgres.rs only. Preserve simultaneous-lifetime, concurrency, lingering-connection, external-mode, explicit-cleanup, and fallback-cleanup behavior.

## Validation

## Acceptance Criteria
The integration suite still uses one amortized container; cleanup resource lifetimes are structural rather than a manual drop ledger; cleanup counters are exact; all existing lifecycle scenarios remain covered.

title: S13: Revalidate stale databases after acquiring their lock
description:
## Verdict
Recommend as a concurrency/state correction. Audit rank 3. High impact and confidence; medium effort and blast radius.

## Evidence
- src/harness.rs:591 snapshots all database rows once.
- src/harness.rs:598-610 classifies snapshot records before locking.
- src/harness.rs:611-622 acquires the snapshot key, then drops and counts without rereading.
- src/admin.rs:324-330 uses DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS.

## Current complexity
A snapshotted Initializing template can become Ready or fresh before lock handoff. Metadata can move to another protecting key. Two sweepers can both count the same database after DROP IF EXISTS.

## Target
Treat the initial scan as a hint. After acquiring the candidate key, use S08-A's exact lookup, rerun the existing classifier, require the current key to equal the held key, and only then drop/count. Reuse CleanupClassification where practical; avoid parallel candidate/outcome type hierarchies unless needed for centralized unlock handling.

## Scope and risks
src/harness.rs plus the S08-A private admin lookup. Always release the originally acquired key on every path. Account for an extra query, disappeared/changed rows, error precedence, and observable CleanupReport counter changes.

## Validation
Add finalized/refreshed metadata races, key change, row disappearance, two concurrent sweepers, unchanged candidate, and unlock-on-error cases.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Snapshot an old managed database as a cleanup candidate.
2. Keep its advisory lock held so the sweeper waits or skips before deletion ownership is authoritative.
3. Refresh/finalize the same resource, or let another sweeper delete it, before the original sweep acquires the snapshot key.
4. Observe that the current code drops/counts from the stale snapshot without an exact locked reread.

## Acceptance Criteria
The locked reread is authoritative; a changed/fresh/ready/missing/key-mismatched database is not dropped or falsely counted; two sweepers cannot both report one drop; lock release and error paths are validated.
acceptance_criteria: The locked reread is authoritative; a changed/fresh/ready/missing/key-mismatched database is not dropped or falsely counted; two sweepers cannot both report one drop; lock release and error paths are validated.
close_reason: Added authoritative exact reread after candidate-lock acquisition, rejected changed/fresh/finalized/missing/key-mismatched rows, guaranteed unlock attempts with primary-error precedence, and validated concurrent sweepers plus Docker lifecycle coverage.

title: S08-B: Centralize managed database creation and tag compensation
description:
## Verdict
Recommend as ownership simplification plus an explicit behavior correction. Audit rank 4. High impact and confidence; medium effort and blast radius.

## Evidence
- src/admin.rs:310-322 creates a database.
- src/admin.rs:359-371 writes managed metadata.
- src/harness.rs:350-360 creates a template and tags it without compensation.
- src/harness.rs:464-475 repeats create/tag with local compensation for disposable databases.

## Current complexity
Callers own different halves of one postcondition. A successful CREATE followed by failed COMMENT can leave an unrecognized deterministic database.

## Target
Add a private create_managed_database operation that owns CREATE -> COMMENT -> compensating DROP after confirmed post-create failure. Do not call it atomic or absorb later Initializing -> Ready transitions. PostgreSQL CREATE DATABASE is not transaction-block compatible, so process-crash exposure remains.

## Scope and risks
src/admin.rs and both callers in src/harness.rs; src/error.rs only if a compound cleanup error is required. Preserve the original failure, define cleanup-error precedence, compensate only after confirmed creation, and be explicit about FORCE-drop behavior.

## Validation
Inject metadata-write failure, prove successful compensation, characterize failed compensation and source preservation, and verify no untagged residue remains.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Allow CREATE DATABASE to succeed for a template or disposable database.
2. Force the subsequent COMMENT ON DATABASE metadata write to fail.
3. On the template path, observe the untagged deterministic database remains.
4. Retry template acquisition and observe conservative InconsistentMetadata handling of the residue.

## Acceptance Criteria
Both managed creation callers use one private operation; successful return guarantees a tagged database; confirmed post-create tagging failure attempts cleanup; original and cleanup errors follow a documented policy; failure-path integration coverage exists.
acceptance_criteria: Both managed creation callers use one private operation; successful return guarantees a tagged database; confirmed post-create tagging failure attempts cleanup; original and cleanup errors follow a documented policy; failure-path integration coverage exists.
close_reason: Centralized CREATE/COMMENT/forced-DROP compensation for templates and disposable databases, preserved tagging errors with compound cleanup reporting, added deterministic policy tests and PostgreSQL failure injection, and passed all verification gates.

title: S12: Return DatabaseLease directly and remove CancellationGuard
description:
## Verdict
Recommend. Audit rank 5. Medium impact, high confidence, low effort and blast radius.

## Evidence
- src/harness.rs:157-204 gives DatabaseLease its fallback cleanup Drop.
- src/harness.rs:223-249 defines a generic CancellationGuard with another armed Option.
- Its sole production use is src/harness.rs:477-484.
- src/harness.rs:487-492 immediately dismantles it and reconstructs DatabaseLease.
- src/harness.rs:697-732 characterizes abandoned blocking-task output cleanup.

## Current complexity
Two separately armed drop owners model the same cancellation behavior, and the lease is needlessly deconstructed/reconstructed across the blocking boundary.

## Target
Compute the name and database URL before the SQL side effect, construct and return the complete DatabaseLease inside the blocking closure, and rely on its existing Drop when a detached task result is discarded. Remove the generic CancellationGuard.

## Scope and risks
src/harness.rs and its unit test; no public API change. Preserve permit lifetime, fallback-worker behavior, explicit cleanup, and detached spawn_blocking output destruction.

## Validation
Replace the generic-guard unit test with a test-local Drop probe and retain real lease cancellation/fallback and explicit-cleanup integration coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria
CancellationGuard has no production role; blocking creation returns a complete DatabaseLease; abandoned output triggers exactly the existing lease fallback cleanup; permit and explicit-cleanup behavior remain validated.

title: S15-A: Make the synchronous postgres crate dev-only
description:
## Verdict

## Evidence

title: S07: Shut down each retained admin runtime directly
description:
## Verdict
Recommend. Audit rank 7. Medium impact, high confidence, low effort and blast radius.

## Evidence
- src/admin.rs:80-117 gives each AdminClient a tokio_postgres client, connection task, and current-thread Runtime.
- src/admin.rs:22 and 168-199 use a process-global OnceLock, channel, permanent drop thread, and mem::forget fallbacks solely for destruction.
- PersistentClient at src/admin.rs:149-165 is the retained advisory-lock owner.

## Current complexity
A global worker exists to destroy independently owned runtimes. Worker start/send failure deliberately retains the client, socket, and potentially a session advisory lock.

## Target
Add consuming AdminClient::shutdown_background(self), destructure/drop client and task in a defined order, then consume Runtime::shutdown_background. PersistentClient::drop invokes it. Remove CLIENT_DROP_WORKER and its channel/thread. Keep PersistentClient's Option because Drop legitimately needs move-out ownership.

## Scope and risks
src/admin.rs only, aside from any S15-A import normalization. Verify connection-task termination, lock release timing, drops from both Tokio runtime flavors, and the assumption that the private runtime has no spawn_blocking work.

## Validation
Add current-thread and multithread Tokio drop cases and an integration assertion that a session advisory lock becomes acquirable after PersistentClient drop.

## Acceptance Criteria
CLIENT_DROP_WORKER, its channel/thread, and mem::forget paths are removed; direct shutdown is safe inside both Tokio runtime flavors; retained session locks are released on drop; no public signature changes.
acceptance_criteria: CLIENT_DROP_WORKER, its channel/thread, and mem::forget paths are removed; direct shutdown is safe inside both Tokio runtime flavors; retained session locks are released on drop; no public signature changes.

title: S10: Pair container shutdown sender and worker handle
description:
## Verdict
Recommend. Audit rank 8. Medium impact, high confidence, medium effort, low-to-medium blast radius.

## Evidence
- src/server.rs:161-165 stores command sender and JoinHandle in separate Mutex<Option<_>> fields.
- src/server.rs:219-228 uses a one-variant command with a second result channel.
- src/server.rs:246-250 initializes the two halves independently.
- src/server.rs:255-285 consumes them through separate error-prone shutdown phases.
- Drop and atexit reuse shutdown at lines 289-355.

## Current complexity
Split fields permit commands=None/worker=Some after an early removal/reporting error, can defer joining, and duplicate the worker result through a reply channel.

## Target
Use one Mutex<Option<ContainerWorker { shutdown: Sender<()>, handle: JoinHandle<RemovalResult> }>>. Signal and join through one serialized terminal transition. A Sender<()> and result-bearing handle should replace the one-variant command/reply protocol. Do not build a generic background-worker framework.

## Scope and risks
src/server.rs. Preserve concurrent idempotence/blocking, startup failure cleanup, removal error sources, worker panic/channel closure, Drop, atexit, and fallback logging when no owner was constructed.

## Validation
Cover successful, failed, repeated, and concurrent shutdown; worker panic/channel closure; startup timeout cleanup; Drop; and subprocess exit cleanup.

## Acceptance Criteria
ContainerOwner has one paired terminal worker state and one serialized shutdown transition; removal results come from the worker handle; all explicit, concurrent, Drop, startup-failure, and process-exit behaviors are characterized.
acceptance_criteria: ContainerOwner has one paired terminal worker state and one serialized shutdown transition; removal results come from the worker handle; all explicit, concurrent, Drop, startup-failure, and process-exit behaviors are characterized.

title: S09: Close connection admission on owned shutdown
description:
## Verdict
Recommend as a lifecycle correction. Audit rank 9. Medium impact, medium-high confidence, low effort, medium blast radius.

## Evidence
- src/server.rs:47-49 and 108-120 own the semaphore and permit acquisition.
- Error::ConnectionBudgetClosed exists at src/error.rs:95-96.
- src/server.rs:133-138 removes an owned container but never closes admission.
- PostgresHarness::shutdown(&self) at src/harness.rs:69-72 leaves clones available.

## Current complexity
Queued or later callers can receive permits after the owned server is removed and then contact a dead endpoint; the closed-budget error is unreachable.

## Target
Close the existing semaphore before terminal owned-container shutdown. External shutdown remains a no-op. Do not introduce a server state enum for this single transition.

## Scope and risks
src/server.rs and observable shutdown behavior. Decide and document whether failed container removal still makes admission terminal. Characterize active permits, clones, repeated/concurrent shutdown, and external mode.

## Validation
Saturate the budget, park a waiter, shut down, and require prompt ConnectionBudgetClosed. Add active-lease, repeated/concurrent, failed-removal, and external no-op cases.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure a budget that can be fully consumed by one live DatabaseLease.
2. Start a second database request so it waits on the semaphore.
3. Call owned PostgresHarness::shutdown while clones and the waiter remain.
4. Release the first permit and observe the waiter can be admitted only to contact the removed server instead of receiving ConnectionBudgetClosed.

## Acceptance Criteria
Owned shutdown closes admission and wakes queued permit requests with ConnectionBudgetClosed; external shutdown does not close admission; failure/repeat/concurrency semantics are documented and tested.
acceptance_criteria: Owned shutdown closes admission and wakes queued permit requests with ConnectionBudgetClosed; external shutdown does not close admission; failure/repeat/concurrency semantics are documented and tested.
close_reason: Completed: owned shutdown closes admission before terminal removal with tested failure and concurrency semantics
